items.topic: Tax-filing form for your own salary above USD 50,000
items.gap: Announcement 2013 No. 40 lists a foreign individual's China work pay among payments needing a tax filing when a single payment exceeds USD 50,000, but its Article 4 sends a foreign individual's own outward payments to the individual FX rules. Which one your bank applies was not confirmed.
items.action: Ask the bank before the visit whether it wants the tax-filing form (服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表) for a single wire above USD 50,000.

items.topic: HSBC China exchange rate
items.gap: HSBC China's CNY/USD selling rate was not obtained, so the FX margin for the HSBC route is blank and no HSBC all-in total is shown.
items.action: Read the rate on the HSBC China app at the time of the transfer and compare it with the Bank of China board.

items.topic: Other mainland banks (ICBC, CCB, ABC, CMB and others)
items.gap: No official tariff page of these banks was opened; only third-party pages were found. All cost cells for this route are blank.
items.action: Open the bank's own published tariff (服务价目表) and its rate board.

items.topic: Intermediary-bank deductions
items.gap: If full-amount delivery is not chosen, overseas banks may deduct charges from the wire. Bank of China states that overseas bank charges are collected as incurred; no figure is published.
items.action: Choose full-amount delivery (USD 25 at Bank of China) or ask the bank which correspondent it uses.

items.topic: US receiving-bank fees other than Chase
items.gap: Only Chase's incoming-wire fee was read on the bank's own page. A Schwab figure was seen only in a search excerpt and is left blank.
items.action: Check your own bank's fee schedule for incoming international wires.

manual.label: Schwab pricing guide (wire row not reached)

items.topic: Wise quotes and limits
items.gap: Wise publishes no fixed tariff for CNY: the figures here are five live quotes from Wise's own comparison API taken on 2026-11-11 between 02:35:43Z and 02:35:50Z. An amount between two quoted points has no figure, and any fee charged by the receiving bank is outside the quote. These comparison-API quotes and the BOC board snapshot were taken at different times; they are not personalized executable quotes, and any Wise receiving-bank fee is unknown.
items.action: Get a live quote in the Wise app; confirm you meet the eligibility rules and your overall limit (after-tax China salary).

items.topic: Western Union fees, limits and delivery
items.gap: No fee or limit is published on Western Union's China page, and transfers to a bank account are shown as temporarily unavailable. All cost cells are blank.
items.action: Ask a partner bank branch for the current fee, limit and whether US passport holders are served.

items.topic: Overseas ATM: card-scheme rate and ATM-owner surcharge
items.gap: Bank of China's own fee is published, but the card-scheme exchange rate and any surcharge of the overseas ATM owner were not verified, so no total is shown.
items.action: Check the rate published by the card scheme on the withdrawal day and the surcharge shown on the ATM screen.

items.topic: Cross-border RMB remittance: conversion outside China
items.gap: The rule allowing banks to send an individual's current-account income abroad in RMB was confirmed, but the conversion cost at the receiving bank, and whether a given US bank accepts a CNY wire, were not.
items.action: Ask the receiving bank whether it accepts CNY and at what rate it converts.

items.topic: CNY cash limit of CNY 20,000 per trip
items.gap: Seen only in a search excerpt of a government article that cites PBOC Announcement 〔2004〕 No. 18; the announcement itself was not opened.
items.action: Open the PBOC announcement or the customs notice before relying on the figure.

items.topic: China late-payment surcharge and tax-evasion fines
items.gap: Articles 32 and 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law were seen only in a search excerpt of the tax authority's database page.
items.action: Open the law on the State Taxation Administration database.

items.topic: China tax on bank-deposit interest
items.gap: The Individual Income Tax Law taxes interest at 20%. A separate notice on savings-deposit interest was not opened, so whether interest earned on the account has been taxed is blank.
items.action: Ask the bank for an interest statement and check with the tax authority (12366).

items.topic: US treatment of an exchange gain above USD 200, or of an exchange loss
items.gap: Only the statute text of §988(e) was read. The character of a gain above USD 200 and whether a loss on a personal conversion is deductible were not verified.
items.action: Compute the USD value of the CNY when received versus when converted and give both figures to a US tax preparer.

items.topic: FBAR willful penalty: the '50% of the balance' alternative
items.gap: The inflation-adjusted fixed amounts were read in 31 CFR 1010.821. The alternative of 50% of the account balance appears on the IRS page only for assessments before 2016-08-01; the statute itself was not opened.

items.topic: Does a long-resident foreigner get the USD 50,000 annual quota?
items.gap: The FX Regulation defines a 'domestic individual' to include foreigners resident for one continuous year, while the Individual FX Measures define a foreign individual by passport. SAFE's 2024 Q&A applies the annual facilitation quota only to holders of a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card.
items.action: Assume no quota unless you hold the permanent-resident card; ask the bank.

items.topic: US–China tax treaty and dividend withholding
items.gap: Treaty rates and withholding on dividends paid to a US resident were not reviewed.
items.action: Read the treaty documents and IRS Publication 901.

manual.label: IRS China tax treaty documents (not opened by this session)

items.topic: House-sale proceeds: who approves
items.gap: The 2006 Measures say the remittance needs SAFE approval; the Shanghai government FAQ (source: Bank of China) describes handling at the bank. The current procedure text was not opened.
items.action: Ask the bank in the city where the property is registered which procedure applies.

items.topic: Emigrant-transfer eligibility
items.gap: The emigrant-property route is defined for people who emigrated from China. Whether it applies to you depends on your own history, which this guide does not know.
items.action: If you were once a mainland resident, ask the SAFE branch of your former household registration.

items.topic: Bank of China commission base and discounts
items.gap: The 1‰ commission is charged on the 'remittance amount'; this guide computes it on the CNY amount held. Channel discounts are not verified.
items.action: Read the fee shown on the bank's confirmation screen.

items.topic: Exchange-rate snapshot
items.gap: Every FX figure uses one Bank of China board reading: 2026-11-11 10:25:02 Beijing time (buy 666.30, sell 669.11 per USD 100). The board itself states that the rate at the actual transaction applies, so the cost moves with the rate. A 0.1% move is USD 400 on a USD 400,000 transfer. Re-read the board on the day.
items.action: Re-read the board on the day; the percentages move with the rate.

items.topic: Full text of the 2020 Current-Account Guidelines
items.gap: Article 59 of 汇发〔2020〕14号 is relied on as quoted by SAFE's Tianjin branch; the full Guidelines were not opened.
items.action: Read the Guidelines on safe.gov.cn.

items.topic: Bank-level limits on one large wire
items.gap: The rules cap nothing for documented current-account income, but a bank's own channel limits for a single wire were not verified. The cost ladder assumes one wire per amount.
items.action: Ask the branch for its single-transaction limit; two wires double the fixed fees.

items.topic: Tax summary and historical rate snapshot require individual review
items.gap: Prior summaries implied that China tax payment eliminates other tax, a foreign tax credit is automatic, or all exchange gains up to USD 200 are ignored. Those claims need qualification. The cost ladder uses a historical BOC rate, not an executable quote.
items.action: Have a US tax professional assess foreign-currency gain, credit eligibility and filing thresholds; obtain an executable bank quote and confirm the source-of-funds route before acting.

items.topic: Cost-model funding and comparison limitations
items.gap: The BOC model assumes the commission and cable are funded separately in CNY and valued at the BOC midpoint, with USD 25 full-amount service paid separately and a USD 15 Chase fee deducted. The actual commission base, correspondent routing, timing, eligibility and other fees are unconfirmed. The historical Wise estimates omit receiving-bank fees and were not obtained at the same time; neither comparison proves the cheapest route.
items.action: Obtain executable quotes at the same time for the same funded amount and destination, verify actual correspondent and receiver fees, and assess tax separately.
